title: Hot
summary: A hot afternoon, and a red bucket that would not stay empty.
alt: A red bucket filled with freshly harvested potatoes, sitting on bare soil.
body: The sun stayed put. Potatoes came up warm, skins dusty, and the red bucket filled until the handle pressed into the hand.
Nothing about the day was arranged for a picture. The bucket got heavy, the row got shorter, and that was enough to keep.

title: Rinsing
summary: A short clip of hands, water, and what the day brought in.
alt: Hands rinsing a green vegetable under running water in a metal bowl.
body: Before the cooking, there is this. Cold water, a metal bowl, and the small work of rinsing what came in from outside.
The clip is only a few seconds long. The day around it was ordinary, which is why it belongs here.

title: Special Kimchi
summary: Two jars packed and set aside, waiting on time.
alt: Two glass jars of red kimchi standing side by side.
body: Kimchi is mostly patience. The cabbage is cut, salted, and packed, then the jars sit where the light is soft.
These two were the special batch. Lids tight. A note to open them slowly.

title: Potato Harvest
summary: A basket of potatoes, still wearing the field.
alt: A wicker basket filled with unwashed potatoes.
body: The basket came in with soil still caught in the weave. Some potatoes were smooth, some knotted, all of them just dug.
Harvest days are mostly carrying and sorting. The photograph is the quiet part at the end.

title: Happy Farming
summary: A good day in the rows, with a handful of new potatoes.
alt: A person in a cap holding freshly dug potatoes in a garden.
body: Not every day outside is an easy one. This one was. The plants were up, the light was kind, and there was enough in hand to feel the season moving.
Happy farming, on this page, is one particular afternoon that went well.

title: Late May
summary: Potatoes in from the field, at the end of the month.
alt: Potatoes from the field, soil still on them.
body: The last day of May, and the potatoes were already coming in. Soil still on them. The season had started in earnest.
This is the earliest frame in the journal.
